author: m. a. zimmerman
title: Adam Smith highlights apprenticeships growth and community roles in recent tweets
text:
Rep. Adam Smith, U.S. Congressman representing Washington’s 9th district since 1997, recently shared a series of statements on social media addressing workforce development, support for military service academy nominees, and housing affordability.
On June 23, 2026, Smith highlighted the expansion of apprenticeship programs in recent years: “Apprenticeships have grown by more than 70% in the past decade, providing a proven pathway to well-paying careers without the cost of a four-year degree. I’ve been a longtime champion of workforce development and wraparound services that help individuals with training, resources,” he wrote.
Later that day, Smith expressed pride in his role nominating candidates to military service academies, “One of the jobs I am most proud of as a member of Congress is nominating brave, smart Washingtonians to our service academies. I had the chance to meet with last year’s academy nominees to hear about the great work they’re doing to support our country’s military. Great work to” (June 23, 2026).
Addressing housing issues on June 24, Smith stated simply, “It should be easier for working families to buy homes.”
Smith has represented Washington’s 9th District since succeeding Randy Tate in Congress and previously served in the Washington State Senate from 1991 to 1997. He was born in Washington, D.C., in 1965 and currently resides in Bellevue at age 57. Smith earned his BA from Fordham University in 1987 and his JD from the University of Washington in 1990.
